## Read in data, look at it 

```{r}
covariate_data <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar.csv")
summary(covariate_data)
str(covariate_data)
head(covariate_data)

gene_expression_data <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
summary(gene_expression_data)
str(gene_expression_data)
head(gene_expression_data)

gene_names <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
summary(gene_names)
str(gene_names)
head(gene_names)

```
what do I notice about the data?

the covariate data has one subject per row and the columns are the covariates (long data)
the data is character strings, will need to remove text and keep numerical values
will also need to code for preeclampsia vs. normal and asthmatic vs. healthy
no missing values

the gene expression data has one subject per column, the rows are the probe ids (wide data)
data is numerical, each column matches a geoid from covariate data (how to match the data)

the gene name data has the gene name corresponding to the probe id (how to match the data)

will need to pivot data



## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
